anatomy.flutter: ActionFeedback wraps a child in a Stack of exactly three layers in paint order: outer shadows, the ramp (linear-gradient(176deg,...) as five OklabColor.mix stops), the Surface (inset shadows, border, label), then two Positioned.fill pseudo-layers (texture, beat), matching CSS's fixed box/background/border/content/pseudo order.
anatomy.web: @utility sheen-action in styles/utilities.css declares position:relative, background-image ramp on the host, ::before (the beat, radial-gradient ellipse, mix-blend-mode) and ::after (the static texture, three background layers at opacity 0.75, mix-blend-mode: soft-light) — three parts, one host class, documented identically in the doc page's 'One class, three parts' block.

api.flutter: ActionFeedback({spec, radius, border, hovered=false, pressed=false, child}) — spec is the ShadowStyle (--shadow-btn-primary/--shadow-btn-down equivalent), hovered/pressed booleans drive which CSS pseudo-rule (:hover::before vs :active::before) is emulated.
api.web: sheen-action is a bare CSS class applied to any host (button.tsx's default variant is the only real consumer today); it has no props of its own — state comes from the host's native :hover/:active pseudo-classes, exactly as the docs 'Usage' section describes (host only needs a background colour and overflow-hidden).

states.flutter: _SheenActionState drives a Ticker-based elapsed-time clock (not a phase-preserving AnimationController) so that changing hovered/pressed re-divides the same elapsed time by a new period exactly like a CSS animation-duration change — documented and measured against the live reference to 4 significant figures (phaseAt/_beatStep).
states.web: &:hover::before runs animation: action-beat var(--duration-beat-hover) infinite (2600ms loop, a double thump then rest); &:active::before runs the same keyframes with animation-iteration-count 1 on --duration-beat-press (620ms) and outranks hover per CSS specificity/source order, per the doc page's Hover/Press rows.

disabled.flutter: action_feedback.dart declares no disabled parameter or branch anywhere in ActionFeedback or _SheenActionState — the effect only reads hovered/pressed.
disabled.web: sheen-action is a decorative CSS class with no disabled variant of its own; the docs' Accessibility section states the beat 'never gates comprehension: nothing about what the control does or whether it is enabled depends on seeing the animation.'
disabled.note: action-feedback is a paint effect layered on a host control (Button), not an interactive control itself, so it carries no independent disabled state on either side — disabled styling belongs to the host, not to this utility.

interaction.flutter: The beat clock starts/stops off hovered/pressed transitions supplied by the caller (Button's Press/Surface plumbing), and the Ticker is only created in initState / running while an animation exists, matching CSS's 'hover-out deletes the animation outright (animation-name: none within 1.4ms of pointerout, measured)'.
interaction.web: &:hover::before / &:active::before are native CSS pseudo-class-driven animations with no JS event handling — pointer hover and mouse/touch press activate them directly through the host element's own state, with :active outranking :hover in the cascade the same way _Beat.press outranks _Beat.hover in phaseAt's repeats:false branch.

semantics.flutter: No semantic label or role is attached by ActionFeedback itself — it is a painting-only StatefulWidget wrapped around child, leaving accessibility to the host Button.
semantics.web: Docs Accessibility section: 'Purely decorative... It never gates comprehension: nothing about what the control does or whether it is enabled depends on seeing the animation' — the effect is unannounced by design on both sides, and reduced motion is a documented n/a-preserving freeze-at-rest (0.01ms, one iteration, falls back to frame 0/opacity:0) rather than a semantics concern.
